Option1: Input alternating-current voltage ranges used by the wall outlet in different regions
Option2: Output direct-current rails to the motherboard

Q: On a manual-input power supply, what happens if the 115 V/230 V selector is set incorrectly for a 230 V region?
Option2: The power supply may be damaged immediately

Q: What do the 3.3 V, 5 V, and 12 V rails represent?
Option2: Separate direct-current output lines used by components

Q: Which components primarily use the 12 V rail today?
Option2: High-current devices such as CPU voltage regulators and graphics cards

Q: What is the purpose of a 20-pin to 24-pin motherboard adapter?
Option2: Allow an older 20-pin power supply to connect to a 24-pin ATX motherboard

Q: What is a redundant power supply in a server chassis?
Option1: Two or more hot-swappable supplies that share load; the system continues if one fails

Q: What is a modular power supply?
Option2: Cables can be connected only as needed to improve airflow and cable management

Q: What does 'wattage rating' of a power supply indicate?
Option2: Total power the unit can safely deliver across all rails

Option3: 550–650 W to allow headroom and future growth

Q: A system randomly shuts down under graphics load. Which power issue is most likely?
Option1: Insufficient wattage or 12 V amperage from the power supply
